name: The Malac Cult (Orthodox)

identity.symbol: A flame-drop pendant — a teardrop of fire
identity.public_perception: The old faith. Respected by elders, ignored by the young. Seen as custodians of something real but diminishing.

goals.primary: Preserve the authentic Malac rite and outlast the schism.
secondary: Maintain the Temple of the Eternal Flame in Dravesa and its counterpart in Orziben.

philosophy.summary: Malac is approached through specific, careful, earned rites — not through spectacle or mass pilgrimage. The Mountain of Fire is real but dangerous and not for everyone. Correct relationship with Malac requires patience and preparation.
methods: Conduct death rites with full preparation
limits: Will not conduct rites at Schismatic sites
Will not publicly acknowledge the Orthodox is losing

position.active_since: Pre-schism; the older of the two Malac traditions in the Luric.

alliances.nature: Pragmatic. Shared opposition to the Schismatics. The Orthodox find the Bandua crude; the Bandua find the Orthodox passive. They work together anyway.

rivals.nature: The schism. The Schismatics have taken most of the young congregation.

needs: Political cover to act against the Schismatics

ilmath.name: Ilmath, High Fire-seer
ilmath.role: The last senior Orthodox cleric in Dravesa or Orziben.

fire-seers.name: The Three Fire-seers
fire-seers.role: Daily temple service and rite. One is quietly attending Schismatic dawn rites.
fire-seers.notes: Unnamed. The wavering one is the crisis.

dm_notes: The Orthodox are dying slowly and know it. Ilmath is the last senior cleric in both settlements — Orziben's died two months ago and she has said nothing. The wavering Fire-seer is the tell that the institution is hollowing out from within.
